limitations.statement: The selected object assumes the h_f interface. An implementation using primitive stochastic derivatives requires a separate construction and verification of its bias, variance and cost.
No convergence theorem, regime-specific schedule, error guarantee, or unrestricted Oracle Complexity conclusion is part of this record.

variants.cost: One h_g interface call, one h_f interface call and one Euclidean projection per update; K+1 of each for the literal inclusive loop. Also two scaled vector updates per step. The primitive sampling, derivative and linear-algebra costs inside the estimators, and the implementation cost of projection, must be charged separately. No primitive total bound is given.

variants.name: TTSA with an explicit biased-hypergradient interface
variants.output: The generated iterate sequence, ending at (x^{K+1},y^{K+1}). Algorithm 1 does not prescribe a convergence-certified selection; no such guarantee is asserted here.
public_inputs: Closed convex nonempty X and Euclidean projection P_X; dimensions d1,d2>=1
Initial pair, nonnegative integer horizon K, supplied positive step sequences alpha_k,beta_k
Estimator procedures with the conditional contract below, finite constants sigma_g,sigma_f and nonnegative nonincreasing bias bounds b_k
variants.query_and_update: At iteration k obtain h_g^k at (xk,yk); set y^{k+1}=yk-beta_k h_g^k. After this update obtain h_f^k at (xk,y^{k+1}) satisfying the F'_k contract; set x^{k+1}=P_X(xk-alpha_k h_f^k). H is an estimator target, not an extra exact-Hessian call prescribed by the abstract algorithm.
variants.requirements: Bilevel objective ell(x)=f(x,y*(x)), y*(x)=argmin_{y in R^{d2}}g(x,y), with source Assumptions 1–2 (src.P054 necessary_context). For the selected Eq.(6) surrogate define H(x,y)=partial_x f(x,y)-partial^2_xy g(x,y)[partial^2_yy g(x,y)]^{-1}partial_y f(x,y). The inner function is C2, unconstrained and uniformly mu_g-strongly convex, mu_g>0. For every k>=0 let F_k=sigma(y0,x0,...,yk,xk), F'_k=sigma(y0,x0,...,yk,xk,y^{k+1}). Require E[h_g^k|F_k]=partial_y g(xk,yk), E[||h_g^k-partial_y g(xk,yk)||^2|F_k]<=sigma_g^2(1+||partial_y g(xk,yk)||^2); E[h_f^k|F'_k]=H(xk,y^{k+1})+B_k with ||B_k||<=b_k; E[||h_f^k-B_k-H(xk,y^{k+1})||^2|F'_k]<=sigma_f^2. Constants sigma_g,sigma_f are finite nonnegative, b_k nonnegative nonincreasing. This is an interface requirement, not a proof that arbitrary primitive samplers satisfy it.
variants.state_and_initialization: Choose (x0,y0) in X times R^{d2}; retain current (xk,yk). Initialize supplied step-size sequences. Algorithm 1 runs k=0,...,K inclusive.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Supply step sequences and finite K, stop after k=K (K+1 updates). The discussion on p.5 motivates alpha_k/beta_k->0 for asymptotic two-timescale sequences. This alone does not certify convergence or a finite-horizon schedule. Regime-specific tuning and polynomial bias decay required by later analyses are outside this interface record.
